# every store under the packages named emptied — a nested package's and a program test's too — so the
# rows after read them cold
cold() { for p in "$@"; do find "packages/$p" -name .avra-cache -prune -exec find {} -delete \; ; done; return 0; }

# build/avra as HEAD's compiler: kept when it was built from this tree's compiler source, else made in
# ONE generation — from the committed seed's link where no compiler stands, else from the one that does
# — with the package libraries beside it, built without building the compiler again. A gate's
# compiler makes no claim of the net, so it is built without it; the two-generation fixed point is the
# build slice's.
compiler() {
    if compiler_stands; then return 0; fi
    if [ ! -x build/avra ]; then row compiler-recover make recover || return 1; fi
    row compiler-gen1 env AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 make avra || return 1
    row compiler-libs env AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 make -o avra libs
}

# what `$1`'s cold build of packages/cli took, in seconds, net on or off by `$2`
cli_built() {
    cold cli
    find "$AVRA_CACHE_DIR" -mindepth 1 -delete
    c0=$(date +%s)
    row "cli-build-$1-cold" env -u AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE AVRA_PROGRAM_NET="$2" build/avra build packages/cli || return 1
    c1=$(date +%s)
    row "cli-build-$1-warm" env -u AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE AVRA_PROGRAM_NET="$2" build/avra build packages/cli || return 1
    echo "cli build net $1: cold $((c1 - c0))s, warm $(( $(date +%s) - c1 ))s" >>"$out/seconds"
    # the warm build's heir waited out, before a row after empties the store it saves
    env AVRA_PROGRAM_NET="$2" build/avra build packages/cli >/dev/null 2>&1 || :
}

#!/bin/sh
# THE CENSUS COMPILER: the cli this tree builds, over a runtime compiled with -DAVRA_CENSUS, written
# to <out>. It counts exactly what the shipping compiler does and never ships: the shipping runtime
# library is rebuilt before this answers, and the cli's own product is gone.
#   sh tools/census_compiler.sh build/avra.census
#
# THE BUILDER IS build/avra unless CENSUS_BUILDER names another: a layout rule is the BUILDING
# compiler's, so a census of a rule builds the census compiler with a compiler that has it.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
out=${1:-build/avra.census}
builder=${CENSUS_BUILDER:-build/avra}
[ -x "$builder" ] || { echo "census: no $builder to build the census compiler with — run \`make avra\` first"; exit 1; }
# A MADE BOX IS NAMED BY ITS CALLER'S CALLER, two frames up, which only frame pointers reach:
# macOS keeps them always, Linux only when asked, in the runtime and in every emitted fn.
counted="-DAVRA_CENSUS -fno-omit-frame-pointer"
shipping() {
    make --no-print-directory build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null 2>&1 || \
        echo "census: the shipping runtime did NOT rebuild — run \`make build/libavra_runtime.a\`"
    find packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll -maxdepth 0 -delete 2> /dev/null || :
}
trap shipping EXIT INT TERM
make --no-print-directory CFLAGS_avra_runtime="$counted" CFLAGS_avra_hot="$counted" build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null
# THE COUNTED LEAVES STAY CALLS: the bitcode the compiler inlines was
# built without the census, so an inlined retain would count nothing.
# THE MINTED BOXES ARE NAMED: each box a runtime row makes is counted by
# its type (AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES), the `type:` table.
# THE CENSUS COUNTS THE COMPILER'S OWN WORK: the old path's check the net runs first is not that work.
AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_FRAME_POINTERS=1 AVRA_INLINE_RUNTIME=0 AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release \
    "$builder" build packages/cli > build/census-build.out 2>&1 || {
    tail -20 build/census-build.out; echo "census: the census compiler did not build"; exit 1; }
# A BINARY THE PROGRAM LAYER PLACES IS ITS KEPT BINARY, LINKED: a census compiler left from an earlier
# run can be that same file, which `mv` will not move onto itself — the old one goes first.
[ ! -e "$out" ] || find "$out" -delete
mv packages/cli/src/main "$out"
# A C symbol wears a leading underscore on macOS and none on Linux.
nm "$out" | grep -Eq '[ _]note_retain$' || { echo "census: $out carries no census — refusing to report"; exit 1; }

    sh tools/census_compiler.sh "$compiler"
fi

src=$out/src
mkdir -p "$src/build"
git archive "$snapshot" | tar -x -C "$src"
cp "$compiler" "$src/build/avra"
find build -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -name '*.o' -o -name '*.a' -o -name '*.so' -o -name 'avra_hot.bc' -o -name 'avra_hot.inc' \) \
    -exec cp {} "$src/build/" \;
printf '%s\n' "$snapshot" > "$out/snapshot"
cache=$root/$out/cache

# One run of the census compiler in the snapshot, once what it reads is older than the stamp window:
# its census to <name>.out, what it printed to <name>.stdout. The machine's store is off unless the
# workload's `store` is `filled`: then on, in the run's own cache, which every cold run starts bare.
counted() {
    name=$1; shift
    machine=0
    [ "${store:-off}" != filled ] || machine=1
    sleep 3
    started=$(date +%s)
    # the census reports at exit only where the run accounts (AVRA_MEM_STATS)
    (cd "$src" && unset AVRA_MACHINE_STORE_DIR && AVRA_MACHINE_STORE=$machine AVRA_MEM_STATS=1 AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$cache" AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1 \
        sh "$root/tools/memcap.sh" "${COST_CAP_MB:-8000}" taskset -c 0 build/avra "$@" \
        > "$root/$out/$name.stdout" 2> "$root/$out/$name.out") || {
        tail -20 "$out/$name.out"; echo "cost: $name failed ($*)"; exit 1; }
    echo "cost: $name $(($(date +%s) - started)) s"
}

# One warm findings run of the cli, its `worked:` line kept as <name>.out, its census beside it.
warm() {
    counted "$1" tapes --findings packages/cli
    mv "$out/$1.out" "$out/$1.census"
    grep '^worked: ' "$out/$1.census" > "$out/$1.out" || { echo "cost: $1 printed no worked line"; exit 1; }
}

# Each edit of the warm lane's table, over the store the cli check left.
warm_edits() {
    warm settle
    cp "$src/$edited" "$out/edited.orig"
    edits | while IFS='|' read -r kind text becomes; do
        [ -z "$text" ] || python3 "$root/tools/cost_ratchet.py" --edit "$src/$edited" "$kind" "$text" "$becomes"
        warm "edit-$kind"
        if [ -n "$text" ]; then
            cp "$out/edited.orig" "$src/$edited"
            warm "back-$kind"
        fi
    done
    find "$out/settle.out" "$out"/back-*.out -delete
}

bare() {
    find "$src" -path '*/.avra-cache*' -delete
    find "$src/packages" \( -path '*/src/main' -o -name '*.av.ll' \) -type f -delete
    mkdir -p "$cache"
    find "$cache" -mindepth 1 -delete
}

workloads | while read -r name store command; do
    bare
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    counted "$name" $command
    [ "$name" != check-cli ] || warm_edits
done
find "$out/cache" "$src" "$out/edited.orig" -delete

#!/bin/sh
# THE EXACT-COUNT GATE'S MEASUREMENT: the census compiler of this tree, run over FIXED workloads whose
# sources are one pinned commit (the `snapshot` row of tools/cost.baseline): cold, each run's census
# kept as build/cost/<workload>.out; and warm after each edit of a fixed set, the answers it worked out
# again kept as build/cost/edit-<kind>.out. tools/cost_ratchet.py judges them.
#   sh tools/cost.sh                      the baseline's snapshot
#   COST_SNAPSHOT=<sha> sh tools/cost.sh  another snapshot (what `make cost-accept` records)
#   COST_COMPILER=<file> sh tools/cost.sh a census compiler already built from this tree
#
# A FIXED INPUT MEASURES THE COMPILER: the snapshot is exported whole, std included, and the census
# compiler stands at its build/avra beside the objects a build links, so every package it reads is
# the snapshot's.
# ONE PROCESS ON ONE CORE DOES ALL THE WORK: a forked worker's counts are its own, so no body is
# lowered ahead (AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF) and the run is held to one core (`taskset`), the width every
# emitter reads, so objects are made in this process by one worker.
# EVERY COLD RUN STARTS BARE: an empty store, and no product a run before it left, which a build reads.
# A FILE IS READ ONLY ONCE IT IS OLDER THAN THE STAMP WINDOW (io.stamp withholds a stamp from a path
# changed in the last two seconds), so what a run stamps never depends on how fast it began.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
root=$(pwd)
out=build/cost
snapshot=${COST_SNAPSHOT:-$(awk '$1 == "snapshot" { print $2 }' tools/cost.baseline 2> /dev/null)}
[ -n "$snapshot" ] || { echo "cost: tools/cost.baseline names no snapshot"; exit 1; }
# A SHALLOW CLONE FETCHES THE ONE COMMIT IT PINS.
git cat-file -e "$snapshot^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || git fetch -q --depth=1 origin "$snapshot" 2> /dev/null || :
git cat-file -e "$snapshot^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || {
    echo "cost: snapshot $snapshot is not in this clone and could not be fetched"; exit 1; }
command -v taskset > /dev/null || { echo "cost: no taskset to hold the run to one core"; exit 1; }

# The cold workloads: a name, the machine's store it runs over, then the command the census compiler
# runs in the snapshot. A STORE IS NOT THE COMPILER: every run but one has the machine's store off, so
# its rows are what the compiler does, whatever a store holds; `cold-with-store-fill` is the cli's
# cold check over an empty store, which it fills — the store's own price, ratcheted apart.
workloads() {
    cat << 'EOF'
check-cli off check --counts packages/cli
build-cli off build packages/cli
check-program off check --counts packages/std-program
cold-with-store-fill filled check --counts packages/cli
EOF
}

# THE WARM RE-RUN WORK OF AN EDIT: over the store the cold cli check left, `tapes --findings` of the
# cli is settled; then each edit of one file is made, the findings run warm and the answers it worked
# out again kept (its `worked:` line), and the file put back and the findings warmed back, so each edit
# meets the store the one before it left. The edits and their file are the warm lane's measured
# table's, so a row reads against its design budget.
# kind|text|what it becomes, `\n` between lines; a noop edits nothing.
edited=packages/cli/src/commands/cache.av
edits() {
    cat << 'EOF'
noop||
inline|//! in, its own verbs. The store is a directory of immutable packs, each the|//! in, its own verbs. The store is a folder of immutable packs, each the
literal|    println("avra cache clean: ${compacted_said(dir)}")|    println("avra cache cleaned: ${compacted_said(dir)}")
comment|    let shared? = machine_layer() else { return 0 }|    // a note\n    let shared? = machine_layer() else { return 0 }
body|    let shared? = machine_layer() else { return 0 }|    let shared? = machine_layer() else { return 0 }\n    let _ = cache_dir().length
signature|fn octets_of(packs: List<PackListed>) -> int {|fn octets_of(packs: List<PackListed>, most: int = 0) -> int {
added|fn cache_dir() -> string {|fn cache_unused() -> int { 3 }\n\nfn cache_dir() -> string {
added_after|fn octets_of(packs: List<PackListed>) -> int { packs.fold(0, (sum, p) -> sum + p.octets) }|fn octets_of(packs: List<PackListed>) -> int { packs.fold(0, (sum, p) -> sum + p.octets) }\n\nfn spare_one() -> int { 1 }
30:# compile doubles what each row costs and proves nothing a row here asks of it. The rows that keep it
62:cost       make cost: the census compiler, cold, over tools/cost.baseline's snapshot; every count within 0.05% of its row
354:slice_cost() { row cost env CENSUS_BUILDER=build/avra make -s -o avra cost; }
445:        cost) slice_cost ;;

content.content:
- `List` has `all`, not `every`.
- A spread's refusals are laws, not pending sugar (`..` is one spelling in a record literal, list, map, variadic seat, call's named seats and pattern): a record spreads only under its type's name (`{ ..a, x: 3 }` is a map: "`..` in a map spreads a map, found `P`"); a record pattern's `..` discards, so `P { x, ..rest }` is "expected `}` to close the `match`"; a list spreads only into its own element type; `f(..xs)` into fixed seats is "`..` spreads into a seat that takes the rest of the arguments"; `is` over a list or record pattern binds only under `if` (`type.is_bind`) and a refutable destructuring `let` needs its `else` (`type.let_pattern`).
- A match arm on the brace's line needs a trailing comma before the next arm ("expected `}` to close the `match`", reported at the second arm); each arm on its own line parses.
- A present-bind arm (`v? -> …`) after a comma-ended arm, or itself ending in a comma, is "expected `}` to close the `match`"; separate such arms by line.
- An empty block as a match arm is an empty map: "a `match`'s arms disagree: `{}` vs the first arm's `void`".
- A `\u` escape is not one: `"\u0041"` keeps its six characters, as do `\0` and `\u{…}` (see Runtime facts); spell a code point with `@std/text`'s `from_codepoint(65533)` and a NUL with `from_codepoint(0)` (sugar backlog: `\u{…}` escapes).
- A bare name in a pattern is a const's or a binder's by its binding, never its spelling: `type.const_pattern` warns when a match ENDS on a const's name and `type.unreachable_arm` when a binder precedes a literal arm (the const-comparison law itself is not pinned here; features/enums/tests/const_pat_template is).
- A match arm whose body is a bare statement (`.Bad(t) -> fail E.Bad(t),`) fails the whole file ("expected `}` to close the `match`"); brace it.
- `get(i)?.name` and `shell(line)?.run()` lex as `?.` ("`?.` reaches into a nullable, this is `Result<…>`"); write `(get(i)?).name`.
- `export let` is "`export` marks a fn, type, enum or trait — not this statement"; `export const` lands.
- A `mut` seat cannot be assigned whole, by design: "a seat is written along a path, never replaced whole" — use a `Cell<T>`, a path write, or answer the new value.
- Two top-level consts of one name are "defined more than once"; a `let` of that name shadows from its line on, and a fn body reads the const.
- `fail` inside a `catch` arm's block is "a `catch` arm answers the ok side"; write the statement `match`.
- `[null, null]` names no type where no seat names one ("a list element takes its type from its value"); any typed sibling or seat names it.
- A keyed list (`list xs by it.id { x -> … }`) is "`list` takes no head value"; reconciliation is positional — not pinned (needs `@std/ui`).
- `derived x = …` and `query x = …` are "expected BREAK"; recompute in a `fn` or hold a `state`.
- `@model type` is "`model` is not defined"; a plain `type` until the derive exists.
- A built-in type name is no domain type: `type Task = { … }` is "`Task` is a built-in type".

Wants the typer does not carry yet:
- A declaring annotation's argument is a literal or a const naming one: `@traced("a" + "b")` is "`traced` generates declarations, so its arguments come from the source alone" — not pinned (needs a package with `@std/meta`).
- `Traced<E>`'s `cause`/`context`/`trace` stay inherent methods permanently (a trait member's answer is fixed by its signature); the real want is a bound on a type's own parameter.

- Two top-level consts of one name are "defined more than once"; a `let` of that name shadows from its line on, and a fn body reads the const.
- `fail` inside a `catch` arm's block is "a `catch` arm answers the ok side"; write the statement `match`.
- `[null, null]` names no type where no seat names one ("a list element takes its type from its value"); any typed sibling or seat names it.
- A keyed list (`list xs by it.id { x -> … }`) is "`list` takes no head value"; reconciliation is positional — not pinned (needs `@std/ui`).
- `derived x = …` and `query x = …` are "expected BREAK"; recompute in a `fn` or hold a `state`.
- `@model type` is "`model` is not defined"; a plain `type` until the derive exists.
- A built-in type name is no domain type: `type Task = { … }` is "`Task` is a built-in type".

Wants the typer does not carry yet:
- A declaring annotation's argument is a literal or a const naming one: `@traced("a" + "b")` is "`traced` generates declarations, so its arguments come from the source alone" — not pinned (needs a package with `@std/meta`).
- `Traced<E>`'s `cause`/`context`/`trace` stay inherent methods permanently (a trait member's answer is fixed by its signature); the real want is a bound on a type's own parameter.

Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   Fri Nov 20 03:22:29 2026 +0000

    grammar: a method call writes its own type arguments after its name, `b.m<T>(a)`
    
    The postfix rule gains `.name<T, …>(…)` ahead of the plain call, built by `method_pinned_written`,
    which keeps the written types in the store's column for the type arguments an expression writes after
    its name (a literal's already). Typing pins the method's own parameters from them, past the impl's,
    before the arguments, the seat and the defaults; a call writing more than the method declares is
    refused as a free call's is. Lowering pins the unit the same way, the formatter prints them, and the
    old path sets the form aside (`NewOnly.PrefixArgs`). Every .av in the tree reads the same under the
    compiler before the rule and after: 4492 files, the same 209 differing and 7 refused under both.
    Witnesses: builds_generic_method_prefix (`b.n < 3` still a comparison), generic_method_prefix_counted.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

its own `"}"` all the same. AND A RAW BODY OPENED INSIDE A HOLE pays
  the hole's count too: the opener was counted against the enclosing
  hole when emitted, and the closer never passes through it. Line
  comments inside a raw body are the generated program's — a `}` in
  one ends nothing.
- A NAME-KEYED TABLE CROSSES MODULES. `impls_named` answers every
  `impl` filed under a NAME (the Decl relation's name bucket), so asking `@std.meta.Code`'s methods signed
  the compiler's own `impl Code` and dragged `features` into a
  derive's resolve. A consumer of such a table filters by what the
  impl's FILE can name (`aims_at`: `visible(file).types`), which
  needs no resolve. And the RECEIVERS pass is the third whole-program
  pass guarded against running inside a resolve (docs/2026_09_21_COMPILER.md §5).
- Grammar authoring: a greedy star cannot be told to stop early. An
  arm that could also START the star's required tail (`_` is a
  NAME; a keyword is a NAME) must be an ordered choice INSIDE the
  repeated slot, anchor-first — never a tail after the star. The
  builder then owns the law the grammar cannot state (exactly one,
  last).
- Grammar authoring: `@expect` attaches only at a sequence's (or a
  repeated group's) TAIL. A MID-sequence `@expect` fails the DSL
  parse of the WHOLE assembly, and the symptom points everywhere
  but home: every feature cascades "references undefined rule
  `expression`" / "builder never called" defects, and the offending
  fragment is never named. (Probed landing `if let`.)
- Grammar authoring: a STATEMENT ends at `END`, never at `BREAK` —
  `END` is the engine's terminal for "a BREAK consumed, or a `}`
  left for the body that opened it", and `@recover(sync_to:
  "END")` stops before that `}` too. That is what lets every body
  (`( s:stmt | BREAK )*`) take a one-line form (`for v in xs {
  out.push(v) }`) with no second grammar; a tail spelled BREAK
  would refuse the one-liner and, with a recovering floor, eat the
  brace (the trap that once forced `"{" BREAK` anchors).
- Grammar authoring: an `@expect` is a HOLE-HIT, not a break — a
  branch that reaches its @expect'd item stands as matched (with a
  hole), and later alternatives are never tried. So an alternative
  meant to catch what an earlier branch cannot must be tried FIRST,
  or the earlier branch must require a distinguishing prefix before
  its @expect'd tail (the map requires `key :` before its `}`, so a
  block can follow as the fallback; the empty map is its own
  branch). And the LINE LAW lives in the lexer: breaks are dropped
  directly inside `(`/`[` and after a continuing operator — a
  grammar never spells `BREAK?` for those.
- Grammar authoring: @recover converts a COMMITTED miss into a HIT
  (a hole, synced to END), and a hit ends the ordered choice, while
  a plain break only DEFERS it — later alternatives still try. So
  among branches sharing an anchor keyword, ONLY THE LAST may
  recover; the earlier ones fail as breaks so the anchor's floor can
  try. `let _`, `let x? … else` and `let x` all anchor on `let`:
  recovery lives on the plain `let` alone (a `@recover` on the `_`
  branch swallowed every let line — 352 tests). And a NAME-headed
  branch (assignment) must stay non-committing — recovery there
  write the new grammar in the OLD spelling, SAVE the standing
  binary aside (`cp build/avra build/avra.pre`), build the product
  with it, rewrite the tree by script, build again with the
  product, gate. The product refuses the old form, so a broken
  product leaves no compiler — the saved copy is the way back. And
  the script must never cross a SYMLINK into another tree
  (`packages/std-cli` was one, into bs2's source, and the rewrite
  changed bs2's file; it is a real file now).
  AN ADDED GRAMMAR ALTERNATIVE IS ONE, and its failure is worse than
  a rewrite's. Adding a branch that shares a leading terminal with an
  existing one is a defect in the ASSEMBLED grammar — "branches 1 and
  2 both begin with STRING — branch 2 is unreachable" (grammar/
  first.av) — and only the PRODUCT assembles it, so the first `make
  avra` SUCCEEDS: the standing binary knows nothing of the new rule.
  The second build refuses, and by then the first has already
  replaced `build/avra`, so the product refuses ITS OWN grammar and
  the lane has no compiler at all. The tree is fine; the compiler is
  broken, which is the reverse of a rewrite's failure. That is what
  makes `cp build/avra build/avra.pre` the whole protocol rather than
  a nicety — the HTTP lane's strings slice paid for this and its way
  back was a copy of ANOTHER LANE's product.
- ITS MIRROR, AND IT POINTS THE OTHER WAY: A REGISTRY ROW THE
  COMPILER'S OWN SOURCE DECLARES CANNOT BE GATED IN THE COMMIT THAT
  ADDS IT. A declaration naming an `rt_sigs` row is legal only to a
  compiler that ALREADY CARRIES the row — `crossing_law` exempts a
  row's name by asking its own `rt_sigs()` — so a tree that adds the
  row and declares it in the same breath is refused by every compiler
  that could build it: the standing binary, the committed seed, and
  therefore `seed-check` and `make bootstrap` alike. THE BRANCH CANNOT
  GATE BY CONSTRUCTION, and the first buildable point is a tree
  carrying BOTH the row and a seed that knows it.

is one `./avra build packages/cli` and one `cp` over `build/avra`
  while the shim execs the binary already on disk (the Makefile's
  `avra` target). THE GENERATION IS THE LAW AND "THE SECOND BUILD" IS
  ITS CONSEQUENCE: change the recipe and the count goes stale while
  the rule does not. So a product built
  right after merging a memory-pass fix carries the fix as SOURCE
  but its own body was compiled by the pre-fix pass — it runs with
  the bug it knows how to fix. Lane A's loop-condition fix merged
  so: my product compiled the suite at 7 GB (main's at 1.2 GB), and
  its second build was killed at 4.2 GB — the leaky product could
  not even compile the cli.
  AND THE FRONT END IS THE SHARPER HALF, because there the first
  build PASSES. THE BUILD THAT SUCCEEDED WAS THE BUILD THAT LIED
  (the sqlite campaign's bitwise lane, three times in one slice): the
  standing binary knew nothing of `>>`, so it compiled the change
  happily; the failure arrived on the NEXT build, when the compiler
  that had learned to munch `>>` read `workspace.av` and lexed
  `Table<List<string>>`'s closing brackets as a shift. `make
  bootstrap`, not `make avra`, was the way out each time. A lane
  touching the LEXER must not read the codegen wording and conclude
  the rule is not theirs.
  AND A DIAGNOSTIC IS THE THIRD KIND, which this wording did not
  reach either: a refusal ADDED to the compiler fires on the
  compiler's OWN SOURCE during the very build that adds it. Making
  the declaring path speak turned a benign re-entry — a memo cycle
  the design calls "a recursive view that contributes nothing" —
  into two refusals of `@derive(Rebuild)` in core/nodes.av, and the
  source that fixes the CAUSE (a cycle wearing `Trap`'s name) could
  not be compiled by the only binary that had the voice. Not the
  seed, which is older; not `make avra`, which reproduces the
  refusal. THE WAY THROUGH IS THE GENERATION THAT DOES NOT YET
  SPEAK — a saved product from before the voice — which compiles the
  source silently and yields one carrying both the voice and the
  honest cause. So a change that makes the compiler SPEAK about a
  construct its own source contains is self-referential exactly as a
  syntax change is, and `cp build/avra build/avra.pre` is the whole
  protocol for it too.

content.content:
Design for `impl_param_bound`, which the lead asked for before any build:

<to_controller>DESIGN impl_param_bound (`impl Respond for Created<T: Shown>`); no build until you say go:
1. Grammar. The impl head's target-argument list takes `type ( ":" bound:type )?` per argument (a new `impl_arg` rule used only inside `Name<…>`), so `T: Shown` and `List<int>` both read. No new statement branch, so no shared-leading-terminal risk; the FIRST-set check still runs on gen-2. A bound on a non-parameter argument (`List<int: X>`) is refused.
2. Storage. The bounds ride a side column like `struct_targs`, no `ImplDecl` shape change. The formatter prints them.
3. Signing. item_methods' `target_bounds` today reads the TYPE's declared bounds when the impl writes none; the impl's own written bounds take that slot (impl first, then type). They then reach every method's `FnSignature.bounds`.
4. Body: yes, a bare impl's body (`impl Created<T: Shown> { … }`) sees `T`'s trait methods, through the same `Signing.bound_of` a free fn's body uses. So `self.value.shown()` types, and an unbounded `T` still refuses "has no known methods".
5. Calls. A method call holds the impl's bound on the receiver's argument, via the `bounds_held` door `applied` already runs (`Created { value: "s" }.response()` → "`string` does not implement `Shown`"). Lowering keys a bounded parameter's unit by its fill, as a fn's are.
6. Old path: NewOnly.ImplBound (it refuses the form). The subset line "`impl T<K: Tr, V>` is expected `{`" and its case go in the same change.
7. Protocol: build/avra saved aside, gen-1 then gen-2, the whole tree re-read under the old vs new compiler (as for `b.m<T>`), witnesses red/green.
Meanwhile: (a) and (b) are committed: 40526134 (instance settings meet their fields, witness instance_setting_mistyped) and 809141ab (phantom param refused, help `Qd<T, …>`; a default applies; witnesses red before, refused after). Full receipts on 809141ab are running (~2 h). Next I'm starting lambda_seat_pinned_by_earlier_arg in a separate worktree.</to_controller>

Both hold, so an impl can narrow what it accepts but never loosen the type's own law. Add an attack: a type `Box<T: A>` with `impl Tr for Box<T: B>` requires A and B, and a T meeting only B is refused. Everything else as designed. The lambda-seat work is fine as described.

#!/bin/sh
# THE PROGRAM LAYER REFUSES WHAT THE OLD PATH REFUSES, IN ITS WORDS, AND BUILDS WHAT IT BUILDS.
# Each case under tools/program-refusals/ is a package of its own:
#   refuses.expected — the source must be refused: the old path's `check` and the program
#     layer's `build` each exit 1, and what each says, its warnings aside, is exactly this text;
#   prints.expected — the source must not be refused: the old path's `check` exits 0, the
#     program layer builds it, and what the product prints is exactly this text;
#   target — a case for another target, its triple: each path BUILDS it for that target, the build's
#     refusal is its words, and a printing case's module runs under node (`tools/run_wasm.mjs`); on a
#     machine with no toolchain for the target, both paths refuse in the toolchain's same words, exit 2,
#     and the case is said untooled, neither held nor failed;
#   warns.expected — beside either: each path's warnings, their first lines in the order said, are
#     exactly this text (for a case only the program layer builds, that layer's warnings); an
#     empty one says no warning is said;
#   differs.why — the paths are known to differ on it, for the reason written there: it is said
#     and not failed while it differs, and FAILS once it holds, until the file is taken away.
# A case that uses a form only the program layer builds (`avra tapes <case> --new-only`) is never
# asked of the old path, which never learned the form: the program layer alone is held to the
# expectation, and the count of such cases is said.
# Every case is copied to a directory of its own with no store and a machine store of its own, so
# each judgement is cold; a path into that copy is said as `<case>`. Prints each failing case with what differs, then the
# counts; exits 1 on any failure. With PIN=1, a case holding neither expectation is first given
# the old path's: its `check`'s words where it refuses, else what its `run` prints.
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh [compiler] [case…]   (default build/avra-try, every case)
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh --known   (each case known to differ, and why; runs nothing)
#   sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh --cases   (each case's name, one a line, as the gate deals them)
# A case is a directory holding its `avra.toml` (tools/lib/cases.sh); one that holds none is no case.
# Every case run, each such directory is named; one named on the command line is refused.
set -u
# a store is copied, counted or emptied here between builds, so each build saves its own before it answers
    fi
    if [ -e "$from/warns.expected" ]; then
        grep '^warning\[' "$tmp/$name.new" | cmp -s - "$from/warns.expected" || {
            echo "$name: the program layer's warnings differ from warns.expected" >&2
            grep '^warning\[' "$tmp/$name.new" | diff "$from/warns.expected" - >&2
            return 1
        }
    fi
    if [ -e "$from/refuses.expected" ]; then
        [ "$new" = 1 ] || { echo "$name: the program layer's build exited $new, not 1" >&2; cat "$tmp/$name.new.said" >&2; return 1; }
        cmp -s "$tmp/$name.new.said" "$from/refuses.expected" || {
            echo "$name: the program layer's words differ from refuses.expected" >&2
            diff "$from/refuses.expected" "$tmp/$name.new.said" >&2
            return 1
        }
        return 3
    fi
    [ "$new" = 0 ] || { echo "$name: the program layer refused it ($new)" >&2; cat "$tmp/$name.new.said" >&2; return 1; }
    "$tmp/$name/src/main" >"$tmp/$name.ran" 2>&1 || { echo "$name: its product failed" >&2; cat "$tmp/$name.ran" >&2; return 1; }
    cmp -s "$tmp/$name.ran" "$from/prints.expected" || {
        echo "$name: its product printed otherwise" >&2
        diff "$from/prints.expected" "$tmp/$name.ran" >&2
        return 1
    }
    return 3
}

cd /work/avra && git status --short | sed -n 21,30p; git -c user.name=Claude -c user.email=noreply@anthropic.com commit -q -m "program layer: generic methods — a method declaring type parameters of its own, typed and instanced as a generic fn is

A method is signed under its impl's type parameters and then its own. A call types through the
same door a free call does: the receiver pins the impl's parameters, the arguments and the seat
wanting the answer pin the method's own, then its declared defaults, and its bounds are held
(\`method_params\` reads both off the method's signature). Lowering instances it the same way
(\`instantiated_on\` pins the method's own parameters as \`instantiated_as\` does a fn's), and a
method's \`plain\` reads its seats alone. The layer's generic-method law and miss are gone; the old
path still refuses the form, and \`NewOnly.GenericMethod\` sets it aside.
Witnesses: builds_generic_methods, generic_method_bound_unmet, impl_generic_method (now builds).

Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   Wed Nov 18 20:17:24 2026 +0000

    ctx, step 1: declare, set and read; the frame on the task, back at a block's end and a caught trap
    
    `ctx name: T = v` declares a context at a module's top level, `ctx name = v` sets it for the rest of
    its block, and `ctx.name` reads it: what the nearest set still in force gave it, else its default,
    kept once as a module `state`'s start is. A set ends as its scope does, by every way out of it; a
    caught trap puts back the frame its guard was entered under, in both engines. A context is new-only:
    the old path refuses each form, and the net sets it aside. A context is named and imported as any
    top-level name; its key is a number of its declared symbol, so a library's context wears one key in
    every program that links it. `ctx` is a soft keyword: a binding of that name stays ordinary, but
    `ctx.name` always reads a context, so the soundness walk's own `ctx` is `facts`.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

[link]
# ffi.o is the EXTERN HOST's frame — the evaluator's way to call a

# inside all of them.
objects = ["../../build/llvm_wrapper.o", "../../build/ffi.o"]
# ffi.o resolves the running image's own symbols by name, so a program
# linking this package keeps every symbol in its dynamic table.

2,12c2,23
< # THE PRE-GATE, on worktree /work/gate-wt of /work/avra. Two steps:
< #   sh /work/gate.sh merge <base> [ref|file.bundle:branch]...
< #       checks out <base> (a ref, or file.bundle:branch), merges the rest in order;
< #       a conflict lists its files and stops (the tree is left mid-merge for a decision).
< #   sh /work/gate.sh check [--rc FILE]... [--test FILE]...
< #       the full gate on the worktree's HEAD, one heavy job at a time, every build cold,
< #       every check as non-root user `gate`; GATE_SEED=<compiler> overrides the standing $src/build/avra. --rc runs AVRA_RC_GUARD=1 over a lone program
< #       file (evaluator, native old path, native program layer; output vs its .expected);
< #       --test runs `avra test FILE`. Each --rc case is also wrapped as a package for its
< #       program-layer row, after a positive control that must abort under the guard. Every tools/witness_program_*.sh is run.
< # Prints one table (check | result | detail | wall). Logs in /work/gate-logs/<run>/.
---
> # THE GATE, IN SLICES: every receipt a landing is held to, cut into slices that each run alone in a
> # tree of their own, so N machines run N slices at once and the gate takes as long as its longest
> # slice. A slice builds the compiler of HEAD itself when build/avra was built from anything else,
> # runs every row on the program layer, the net off but where a row's claim is the net, empties the
> # stores a cold row reads, bounds every command, keeps each row's words under build/gate/<slice>/, and
> # ends with ONE line:
> #   GATE <slice> <sha8> PASS|FAIL rows=<n> failed=<n> <seconds>s
> # exiting 0 on PASS, 1 on FAIL.
> #
> #   sh tools/gate.sh list               each slice, one a line, with what it holds
> #   sh tools/gate.sh <slice> [arg]      one slice; the idioms slices take the base sha their diff starts at
> #   sh tools/gate.sh seed               build/gate/compiler-<sha8>.tar.gz: HEAD's compiler — ONE generation, built
> #                                       here first where none of HEAD's stands — and every object a tree
> #                                       links with; `pack` is its other name. Run it once; every slice
> #                                       then starts from `unpack` and builds nothing.
> #   sh tools/gate.sh unpack <file>      seeds this tree from a pack, and holds its stamp to HEAD's: a
> #                                       seeded slice builds no compiler

   - `NewOnly.GenericMethod`.
   - In the SAME change: remove the CLAUDE.md "The subset today" text "a generic method is 'generic methods are recorded, not landed'" (line ~1722) AND its case `compiler/tests/subset/refusals_test.av` "a generic method is refused" (~line 413).

   - Case set (complete per lead): own-param inferred; pinned as a prefix; defaulted; bounded and refused; on a generic impl (<T> + <U>); through a bound; through `dyn` refused; eval == native.

Then: **a foreign generic record literal as a generic fn's TAIL** (services ask, program layer only). "a body not made yet: an untyped record literal `Dead`", while a typed `let` passes. It's an inference gap at a tail seat. Find one case; fix through the one door (likely the body's answer as the literal's `expected` in `fills`, now that the literal door passes `expected`).

- **Sibling pinning:** a sibling arm's type is a seat for an arm that names none, in `if`/`match`/`when`/`??`, for generic calls AND bare variants. Witnesses `sibling_pin_*`, `w_variant_lit_branch` (known to differ). ROADMAP note "A sibling arm's type is a seat for the arm that names none".

- `pw_rest_spread_element`: the layer's element words are kept (don't "fix" `f(1, ..["s"])` to whole-argument words).
- `xs?[0] ?? 0` warning on both paths is correct (propagate-then-index).

- `E.all(1)`, find_map and Pair.made words → parity-words lane. `{}`.length and `[].map` etc. → resolve-2. Don't take them.

## Open asks waiting on others

None blocking. The lead tells the services session when features land.

## Trip hazards

- **Environment:** `. /etc/profile.d/avra.sh` before builds. `make try` builds `build/avra-try` (4–11 min).
- **ONE heavy job at a time:** builds, gate, `check packages/std-avrac` and the cli build. Two at once OOM'd and restarted the container (twice). Never edit `/work/avra` sources while a gate runs: the suite reads them, and that tainted one run.
- **Receipts:** `scripts/rc.sh` runs, in order: make try, layer check std-avrac, probes, cli NET=0, gate a–g, witness, idioms. Summary in `/tmp/rc-sum.log`; it takes ~70–90 min. Delete `/tmp/rc-*.log` before a run, or a wait loop returns on a stale log.
- **Idioms** needs `AVRA_MEM_POOL_MB=13000`; the default pool ran out (exit 2).
- **Witness:** `sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh build/avra-try <cases>`; `PIN=1` writes expectations from the old path.
  - `differs.why` beside a case = known to differ; once it holds, it FAILS until the file is removed.
  - A warning difference needs `warns.expected` (refusals are compared "warnings aside").
  - A form only the layer builds is held on the layer alone (NewOnly).
- **Spec strings:** `${…}` inside a spec's source string must be written `\${…}`, or the spec file interpolates it.
- **Probes and measures:**
  - `scripts/cmp.sh <file.av>` compares old vs layer `check` output.
  - `scripts/warn.py <tsv> <out.json>` is the warnings count; it writes packages to `/tmp/ww/pkg` and symlinks `vendor/<x>` to `packages/std-<x>`.
  - **CAUTION:** `warn.py` reuses ONE directory, so the old path's store can keep a previous row's facts. My census "difference" was that artifact. Use a fresh dir per row for anything delicate.
- **Scratch worktree** `/work/wt`: detached, holds a staged copy of the 0b820238 draft. Reset it before reuse: `git reset -q && git checkout -- .`
- `/work/avra-standing-backup` is an older standing compiler binary (not needed).
- **Bridge:** `mcp__claude-bridge__post_to_controller` with the session token from the brief. Posts: ≤12 lines, numbers first, only at a bundle, a blocker or a ruling. Push nowhere.
- **Bundles:** `git bundle create /work/avra-lane-parity-types.bundle b54/batch54..avra-lane-parity-types` (or against the newest batch), then post `BUNDLE READY <path> <head>`.

   - In the SAME change: remove the CLAUDE.md "The subset today" text "a generic method is 'generic methods are recorded, not landed'" (line ~1722) AND its case `compiler/tests/subset/refusals_test.av` "a generic method is refused" (~line 413).
   - The refusal lives in old `compiler/typing/impls.av:443/601/718` and layer `compiler/item_generic_methods.av`.
   - Case set (complete per lead): own-param inferred; pinned as a prefix; defaulted; bounded and refused; on a generic impl (<T> + <U>); through a bound; through `dyn` refused; eval == native.

Then: **a foreign generic record literal as a generic fn's TAIL** (services ask, program layer only). "a body not made yet: an untyped record literal `Dead`", while a typed `let` passes. It's an inference gap at a tail seat. Find one case; fix through the one door (likely the body's answer as the literal's `expected` in `fills`, now that the literal door passes `expected`).

## Rulings in force (from the lead)

- **Sibling pinning:** a sibling arm's type is a seat for an arm that names none, in `if`/`match`/`when`/`??`, for generic calls AND bare variants. Witnesses `sibling_pin_*`, `w_variant_lit_branch` (known to differ). ROADMAP note "A sibling arm's type is a seat for the arm that names none".
- **Precedence**, one door, a later step never overriding an earlier one: written prefix → arguments → wanting seat (a nullable seat by its present type) → declared default → refused.
- `pw_rest_spread_element`: the layer's element words are kept (don't "fix" `f(1, ..["s"])` to whole-argument words).
- `xs?[0] ?? 0` warning on both paths is correct (propagate-then-index).
- The 40 warning follow-ons in package-245/split-368 close with their errors; leave them.
- `E.all(1)`, find_map and Pair.made words → parity-words lane. `{}`.length and `[].map` etc. → resolve-2. Don't take them.

## Open asks waiting on others

None blocking. The lead tells the services session when features land.

## Trip hazards

- **Environment:** `. /etc/profile.d/avra.sh` before builds. `make try` builds `build/avra-try` (4–11 min).
- **ONE heavy job at a time:** builds, gate, `check packages/std-avrac` and the cli build. Two at once OOM'd and restarted the container (twice). Never edit `/work/avra` sources while a gate runs: the suite reads them, and that tainted one run.
- **Receipts:** `scripts/rc.sh` runs, in order: make try, layer check std-avrac, probes, cli NET=0, gate a–g, witness, idioms. Summary in `/tmp/rc-sum.log`; it takes ~70–90 min. Delete `/tmp/rc-*.log` before a run, or a wait loop returns on a stale log.
- **Idioms** needs `AVRA_MEM_POOL_MB=13000`; the default pool ran out (exit 2).
- **Witness:** `sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh build/avra-try <cases>`; `PIN=1` writes expectations from the old path.
  - `differs.why` beside a case = known to differ; once it holds, it FAILS until the file is removed.
  - A warning difference needs `warns.expected` (refusals are compared "warnings aside").
  - A form only the layer builds is held on the layer alone (NewOnly).
- **Spec strings:** `${…}` inside a spec's source string must be written `\${…}`, or the spec file interpolates it.
- **Probes and measures:**
  - `scripts/cmp.sh <file.av>` compares old vs layer `check` output.
  - `scripts/warn.py <tsv> <out.json>` is the warnings count; it writes packages to `/tmp/ww/pkg` and symlinks `vendor/<x>` to `packages/std-<x>`.
  - **CAUTION:** `warn.py` reuses ONE directory, so the old path's store can keep a previous row's facts. My census "difference" was that artifact. Use a fresh dir per row for anything delicate.
- **Scratch worktree** `/work/wt`: detached, holds a staged copy of the 0b820238 draft. Reset it before reuse: `git reset -q && git checkout -- .`
- `/work/avra-standing-backup` is an older standing compiler binary (not needed).
- **Bridge:** `mcp__claude-bridge__post_to_controller` with the session token from the brief. Posts: ≤12 lines, numbers first, only at a bundle, a blocker or a ruling. Push nowhere.
- **Bundles:** `git bundle create /work/avra-lane-parity-types.bundle b54/batch54..avra-lane-parity-types` (or against the newest batch), then post `BUNDLE READY <path> <head>`.

1	# Avra — clean-room compiler
2	
3	## AVRA PRINCIPLES
4	
5	The spec's Part 0 frames every decision (full text: spec, Part 0).
6	Above all: **P6, paradox collapse** — binary choices are usually false
7	dichotomies; find the design where both sides win. When a trade-off
8	feels forced, the model is wrong, not the requirements.
9	
10	- P1  LLM-first: correct on first generation is the success metric
11	- P2  substrate for autonomous services
12	- P3  gloriously declarative, zero ceremony
13	- P4  Rust-level performance or better
14	- P5  full-stack vertical integration
15	- P6  paradox collapse
16	- P7  visible magic — always inspectable
17	- P8  escape hatches everywhere
18	- P9  boundaries are contracts
19	- P10 the compiler holds semantic knowledge no other tool has
20	- P11 machine-readability is the substrate, human-readability the projection
21	- P12 one source of truth, many projections
22	- P13 collapse dev/ops/infra
23	- P14 no runtime, no framework, no container
24	- P17 composability over featurefulness
25	
26	Clean restart of the Avra compiler, built slowly, one reviewed file at a
27	time. Front end first: an extensible grammar assembled from
28	LanguageFeature components, producing an AST for later passes.
29	Toolchain: the compiler builds itself — `./avra` runs `build/avra`,
30	and a cold tree bootstraps from `bootstrap/seed.ll.gz` (`make bootstrap`;
31	README.md).
32	
33	Design sources of truth (in `../forge-crafting-intepreters`):
34	- `docs/2026_04_18_FULL_SPEC.md` — the language
35	- `docs/2026_06_14_AST_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH_EPIC.md` — node model, spans, error tolerance
36	- `bootstrap/docs/2026_08_19_STANDARDIZATION.md` — front-end shape
37	
38	Follow the old tree's *documented designs*, never its code habits.
39	
40	## Comments
41	
42	Never write comments about specific situations, tickets, approaches, or
43	points in time. Comments are evergreen: always relevant, or absent.
44	Keep them very terse, in plain language. State what a thing is or the
45	invariant it holds — no narration, no self-justification, no history.
46	
47	## The idiom bar — BEFORE writing any fn
48	
49	First drafts are written idiomatic, not cleaned up later. Before
50	the body exists, answer:
51	
52	1. Is any loop a MAP/FILTER/FLAT-MAP? Comprehension (`?` works in
53	   element and iterable; predicates hoist into named fns).
54	2. Building head-plus-tail? `concat` (a list METHOD) / `flatten`
55	   (core's FREE fn — `flatten(xs)`, never `xs.flatten()`), never
56	   push-ceremony.
57	3. Is a projection being spelled twice? The second spelling names a
58	   verb (`cx.int_at`, `expr_fps`) or uses the existing one.
59	4. Does absence read straight? (`?? `, `?.`, if-null early return —
60	   never a two-arm null match without payload logic on both arms.)
61	5. Scanning for one element? `find`/`any`/`index_of`, not a flag
62	   loop.
63	6. Unsure a shape compiles in the subset? PROBE in scratch first —
64	   fear of traps is how ugly-but-safe drafts happen, and every
65	   probe result gets recorded so the fear shrinks.
66	
67	DOGFOODING.md is the full rulebook; `avra check --baseline
68	tools/idioms.baseline` FAILS on any NEW site — the baseline lists
69	sites, never counts, and no tool path can add to it (`make idioms`
70	runs every package, `make idioms-accept` prunes what a fix made
71	gone). Every idiom the language can state is a `rule` declaration,
72	found by `avra check` itself, and the gate counts a RULE's finding
73	only — `type.alias_copy` wears the same `warning[kind]` shape and is
74	the compiler's own law, never a rule, so the gate reads the rule
75	table (`avra rules --json`), never a kind-string shape. Accepted
76	debt lives in the baseline alone, reviewed at adoption and every
77	time after. A new idiom lands in DOGFOODING's registry AT DISCOVERY,
78	named by its rule — `<module>.<rule>`, never a number.
79	
80	## Style
81	
82	- Inline single-use values. A `let` earns its place only when the
83	  name carries meaning the expression lacks, the value is read more
84	  than once, or the subset REQUIRES a pin (a `dyn` value selected
85	  among arms, a Result-answering lambda — "The subset today" names
86	  each). Empty literals (`[]`, `{}`) infer inline in
87	  constructor fields — never bind them to a throwaway name. When a
88	  pin seems needed, probe before assuming.
89	- A state struct's impl is its VOCABULARY: the small verbs that
90	  read or write its tables (`speak`, `bind`, `mint`, `give`) live
91	  as methods, so drivers read as prose. The free state fns the
92	  bootstrap habit left (`eval_node(ev, cx, e)`, the interpreter's
93	  `put(m, …)`, the backend's `define(em, …)`) are methods now, and
94	  so are the pass contexts' whole vocabularies (`cx.accepts(e,
95	  want)`, `cx.open_region(c)`, `ws.sig(d)` — 320 verbs, one sweep);
96	  style.free_state_verb refuses a new free verb in the pass's own files. A PASS ENTRY
97	  POINT (`lower(a: Analysis)`, `memory(l: Lowered)`) keeps the one
98	  standard signature and is not a verb.
99	- A long fn splits at its PHASE boundaries into named helpers, each
100	  with a one-line contract (`match_seq` matches, `built` builds —
101	  grammar/executor.av; `window` frames, `severity_word` branches —
102	  diagnostics/render.av). If a fn needs a paragraph comment
103	  mid-body, that paragraph is a helper's name.
104	- A LAW never assembles PROSE: every refusal is a NAMED VOICE fn
105	  (its whole body the one `spoken`/`emit`), in a voices section at
106	  the file's tail or shared where features share words. Rule
107	  bodies read as guard + verb (rule.compiler.refusal_assembled;
108	  enums/check.av is the exemplar).
109	  AND A VOICE STATES THE LAW, NOT THE SYMPTOM. "a pointer's only
110	  constant is null" is the rule; "both engines read it as null" was
111	  the observation that happened to hold the day it was written. A
112	  symptom-worded refusal goes STALE the moment the mechanism moves,
113	  and until then it reads as a workaround for a quirk rather than a
114	  rule to obey — so it teaches the reader to look for the quirk. The
115	  law's wording outlives its own implementation, which is what makes
116	  it worth pinning in the golden (lower.av's pointer-constant guard).
117	- A BUILDER'S WORDS ARE ITS CLAIM. A builder's refusal is carried
118	  WHOLE into its diagnostic (grammar/executor.av's build phase:
119	  `cause: Cause.Builder, message: m`), so a message that is a LAW
120	  the writer broke reads as the law, and one that is a DEFECT says
121	  so in its own words. A blanket "builder failed:" prefix once told
122	  the reader the compiler had broken about every law — five of the
123	  seven refusals sampled at c7b5038 — while `Cause` had separated
124	  `Builder` from `Defect` all along: the seam was right and only the
125	  WORDING lied. THE GENERAL SHAPE: A PARAPHRASE OF A FLAG IS A
126	  SECOND COPY, and the reader believes the words — the flag is
127	  checked by the code, the prose by nobody. So the WORDS carry the
128	  CLAIM and the STRUCTURE carries the CATEGORY (`Cause.Builder`
129	  projects to F0102, compiler/codes.av), and the words never restate
130	  the category.
131	- A projection is ONE match: nested patterns
132	  (`.Node(.NAlt(a)) -> a, _ -> null`), never an unwrap ladder.
133	- The third copy of a shape names the concept: shared walks and
134	  registries get ONE definition (`post_order`, `file_command`) and
135	  the copies die. Two copies may wait; three never do.
136	
137	## Dogfooding is design
138	
139	The compiler is Avra's first user. When its code WANTS a construct
140	the language lacks — a sugar, a projection, a rule — add the ask to
141	the ROADMAP's sugar backlog, naming the wanting site, as part of the
142	change that hit it. Request your own features: the backlog feeds the
143	spec. The same discipline runs one level down: a PATTERN discovered
144	while writing (a beautiful form, a smell, a licensed exception) is
145	an IDIOM — it lands in DOGFOODING.md's registry at discovery, and
146	the greppable ones become `rule` declarations `avra check` finds
147	directly (compiler/idioms.av, or a feature's own idioms.av). The
148	registry is the idiom engine's spec, written by dogfooding.
149	
150	## Rules
151	
152	- `core/` is infrastructure only. Features never import features.
153	- Layering is one-way: core -> grammar -> features -> compiler, all
154	  over `@std/relation`, whose `engine/` is the memo kernel —
155	  infrastructure, language-agnostic, the one a running program asks too.
156	  `grammar/` is the language-agnostic engine; `compiler/` is the
157	  driver and the ONE definition of Avra (feature order is branch
158	  order is the language).
159	- No string tags or string-matching to detect behavior.
160	- `_ ->` over our own enums is decided by COUNTING THE ANSWERING
161	  ARMS. One arm answers -> a PROJECTION, and the catch-all is
162	  honest: its contract pins the answer for variants that do not
163	  exist yet. TWO OR MORE answer -> a REGISTRY, and a catch-all there
164	  silently forgets the next variant (`let_name` dropped For's
165	  counter exactly so; `type_decl_name` would have swallowed the next
166	  type-declaring statement). Registries spell every arm — `or`-runs
167	  keep that affordable. Ratcheted as style.registry_catchall AND held by the compiler:
168	  F2040 counts the ANSWERING ARMS over the declared enum and names
169	  the variants a hole would forget. The license is a SPELLING, not a
170	  comment — `rest ->` says the remainder is deliberate, and both the
171	  compiler and the ratchet read it. The two licensed shapes are a
172	  feature matching its own variants (it cannot enumerate other
173	  features') and a loop that DELEGATES the rest to an exhaustive
174	  dispatch — each writes `rest ->` at the site.
175	  AND THE LAW IS ABOUT THE TEST, NOT THE MATCH. For a REGISTRY enum
176	  `is .Variant` IS A CATCH-ALL IN DIFFERENT CLOTHES: a boolean that
177	  asks about ONE variant and falls through for the rest discharges
178	  the registry's obligation no better than `_ ->`, and it is harder
179	  to see. For a PROJECTION enum it stays the right idiom. Two
180	  `RtKind` consumers were written that way (`rt_arg`, `answers_word`
181	  in llvm.av), correct only while the enum had three variants —
182	  widening it to carry C's integer widths would have sent an Avra
183	  `int` into an `i32` seat with no truncation, compiling clean. Both
184	  are exhaustive matches now.
185	  ENFORCEMENT SPLITS FROM THE LAW HERE, deliberately: no grep tells a
186	  registry enum from a projection one, so this gets NO ratchet rule.
187	  The keeper is `make vocab`, a CURATED table naming each registry's
188	  consumers and refusing BOTH shapes inside them — the table says
189	  which registries it holds, and a registry it does not name is
190	  unguarded. Naming the next one IS how this law is enforced.
191	  AND THE OBLIGATION CROSSES INTO C, where no keeper can follow. The

1647	- `[i for (i, m) in xs.enumerate()]` — "`enumerate` pairs only under a paired `for` head"; write `[f(i, x) for i, x in xs]`.
1648	- `int??` has no spelling ("expected `)`"/"expected `=`" at the first `?`) though a generic reaches `string??`.
1649	- A bare `table { … }` reads as a struct literal ("no `type table` is declared"); write `table<Row> { id | name … }` with a pipe header.
1650	- A record literal as a component instance's head stands in parentheses (`tally (Span { n: 2 }) { extra: 3 }`); bare, the brace opens the block — pinned by features/components/tests/components_head_test.av, not by this section.
1651	- A semicolon between statements is "unexpected character `;`"; a one-line body is `{ a }`.
1652	- A field's mark on its own line inside a type literal is "expected `}` while parsing `stmt`"; write it on the field's line (`{ @local at: int }`).
1653	- `if let v? = e { … }` takes an `else`: without one it is "expected BREAK" at the `let`; a guard is `let v? = e else { … }`, and a present-only test is `if e != null { … }`.
1654	- A range takes methods (`any`, `find`, `map`, `all`) but has no `.length`.
1655	- A `once fn` takes no type parameters ("expected `(`"), no arguments, and answers a managed value ("`once fn seed` answers `int`, which the runtime cannot keep").
1656	- A trailing block in a head (`if f(a) { x -> x } { … }`) is "expected BREAK"; parenthesise the call. `a?.m { … }` and `(f(a)) { … }` take no trailing block either — not pinned.
1657	- A seat default lands on `fn`, `mut fn`, `static fn` and a trait's `fn` (whose default every impl takes) only: `extern fn` and a lambda refuse it ("expected `)`", "expected `)` to close the group"); a named argument skips a defaulted seat; a default reads no sibling param; a fn value of a defaulted fn wears every seat.
1658	- A generic fn as a value: pinned `ident<int>` is "expected BREAK"; bare is "a generic fn is not a value — no single signature to wear".
1659	- Instantiation is a statement: as a fn's tail it answers `void` — bind, then return the name; a component block is `key: value` ("declares no `List` field, so its block holds settings only") — not pinned.
1660	- A shell `${VAR}` in a string is Avra's interpolation ("`HOME` is not defined", or silently the binding's value); write `$VAR`.
1661	- `_` is a parameter name nowhere ("`_` is a keyword"); an unread seat is `_q`, and `let _ = f()` is the binding spelling.
1662	- A map's keys are strings only ("a map's keys are strings, not `int`").
1663	- `xs ++ ys` is "expected BREAK"; `xs.concat(ys)` or `[..xs, ..ys]`.
1664	- `List` has `all`, not `every`.
1665	- A spread's refusals are laws, not pending sugar (`..` is one spelling in a record literal, list, map, variadic seat, call's named seats and pattern): a record spreads only under its type's name (`{ ..a, x: 3 }` is a map: "`..` in a map spreads a map, found `P`"); a record pattern's `..` discards, so `P { x, ..rest }` is "expected `}` to close the `match`"; a list spreads only into its own element type; `f(..xs)` into fixed seats is "`..` spreads into a seat that takes the rest of the arguments"; `is` over a list or record pattern binds only under `if` (`type.is_bind`) and a refutable destructuring `let` needs its `else` (`type.let_pattern`).
1666	- A match arm on the brace's line needs a trailing comma before the next arm ("expected `}` to close the `match`", reported at the second arm); each arm on its own line parses.
1667	- A present-bind arm (`v? -> …`) after a comma-ended arm, or itself ending in a comma, is "expected `}` to close the `match`"; separate such arms by line.
1668	- An empty block as a match arm is an empty map: "a `match`'s arms disagree: `{}` vs the first arm's `void`".
1669	- A `\u` escape is not one: `"\u0041"` keeps its six characters, as do `\0` and `\u{…}` (see Runtime facts); spell a code point with `@std/text`'s `from_codepoint(65533)` and a NUL with `from_codepoint(0)` (sugar backlog: `\u{…}` escapes).
1670	- A bare name in a pattern is a const's or a binder's by its binding, never its spelling: `type.const_pattern` warns when a match ENDS on a const's name and `type.unreachable_arm` when a binder precedes a literal arm (the const-comparison law itself is not pinned here; features/enums/tests/const_pat_template is).
1671	- A match arm whose body is a bare statement (`.Bad(t) -> fail E.Bad(t),`) fails the whole file ("expected `}` to close the `match`"); brace it.
1672	- `get(i)?.name` and `shell(line)?.run()` lex as `?.` ("`?.` reaches into a nullable, this is `Result<…>`"); write `(get(i)?).name`.
1673	- `export let` is "`export` marks a fn, type, enum or trait — not this statement"; `export const` lands.
1674	- `Result<void, E>` is "a `Result` side cannot hold `void` yet"; a writing verb answers what it wrote.
1675	- A `mut` seat cannot be assigned whole, by design: "a seat is written along a path, never replaced whole" — use a `Cell<T>`, a path write, or answer the new value.
1676	- Two top-level consts of one name are "defined more than once"; a `let` of that name shadows from its line on, and a fn body reads the const.
1677	- `fail` inside a `catch` arm's block is "a `catch` arm answers the ok side"; write the statement `match`.
1678	- `[null, null]` names no type where no seat names one ("a list element takes its type from its value"); any typed sibling or seat names it.
1679	- A keyed list (`list xs by it.id { x -> … }`) is "`list` takes no head value"; reconciliation is positional — not pinned (needs `@std/ui`).
1680	- `derived x = …` and `query x = …` are "expected BREAK"; recompute in a `fn` or hold a `state`.
1681	- `@model type` is "`model` is not defined"; a plain `type` until the derive exists.
1682	- A built-in type name is no domain type: `type Task = { … }` is "`Task` is a built-in type".
1683	
1684	Wants the typer does not carry yet:
1685	- A declaring annotation's argument is a literal or a const naming one: `@traced("a" + "b")` is "`traced` generates declarations, so its arguments come from the source alone" — not pinned (needs a package with `@std/meta`).
1686	- A generic struct literal's field seat unifies instead of planting a want: an unpinned `mk()` there is "`N` is not pinned by the arguments".
1687	- A lambda in a field or argument seat does not read the seat's answer ("`.Ok` needs a known enum"); a typed `let` does, and a named fn works everywhere.
1688	- `Traced<E>`'s `cause`/`context`/`trace` stay inherent methods permanently (a trait member's answer is fixed by its signature); the real want is a bound on a type's own parameter.
1689	- A bound lands on a free fn's and a component's parameters only: `type T<K: Tr, V>` and `impl T<K: Tr, V>` are "expected `=`"/"expected `{`", a generic method is "generic methods are recorded, not landed"; a generic container keyed by a typed id keys by the slot (core's `SideTable`).
1690	- Variant arms or `is` over a nullable enum are "`match` chooses over an enum, found `K?`" / "`is` asks an enum for its variant, found `K?`"; unwrap first.
1691	- A bound method as a value (`xs.any(self.rides)`) is read as a property ("no field `rides` on `S`"); write `(k) -> self.rides(k)`.
1692	- `it` through a self-method wrapper (`xs.any(self.rides(it))`) is "`it` has no element here"; `it` binds to the nearest call, and a pipe stage is such a call.
1693	- `[1, 2].join(",")` is "`join` reads a list of text, this one holds `int`"; map to text first.
1694	- `==`, `contains`/`index_of` and a literal pattern compare a scalar, text, a tagged enum, or a one-field record; two fields is "`==` compares by value — …", and an enum carrying a payload is refused too (help: match on it).
1695	- A named type is opaque at a seat and transparent at a read: a `Rows` seat refuses a computed `List<int>` ("wants `Rows`, found `List<int>`") and takes a literal.
1696	- `r catch null` answers the ok side, so `let x? = r catch null else { … }` is "a `catch` arm answers the ok side: `D`, this is `null`" (and "`x?` asks a nullable"); a `Result` read as absence is a `match` (`.Ok(d) -> d, .Err(_) -> null`).

1698	Methods the runtime lacks:
1699	- `List.reverse()` / `sort()` are "calls a method, and `List<int>` has none"; core's `reversed` is the helper.
1700	- `m["k"]` on a map is "`[...]` indexes a `List`, found `Map<string, int>`"; `.get(k)` answers `T?`.
1701	- `b[0]` on `Bytes` is "`[...]` indexes a `List`, found `Bytes`"; `b.at(i)` reads an octet and traps past the end. `[104, 105].bytes()` answers `Bytes?` ("declares `Bytes`, this is `Bytes?`"), and `.at` on it is refused.

1703	Runtime facts, ours to ratify:
1704	- `split` drops a trailing empty segment and keeps a leading one (`".a"` two, `"a."` one, `""` none).
1705	- `"\u0041".length` is 6, `"ab\0cd".length` is 6 and `"\u{1F600}".length` is 9 — no `\u` or `\0` is an escape.
1706	- A 50000-deep recursion runs in `avra run`; a runaway traps at 100000 nested calls — the trap is not pinned.
1707	- Not gate-pinned: a string's `.length` is a header load; a NUL is an ordinary character in every text verb (`from_codepoint(0)` mints one; `==`, `contains`, `starts_with` walk the header); `parse_int` takes exactly `-`? digits and answers the smallest int whole; `Bytes` text readers (`text()`, `text_prefix()`, `text_lossy()`). Each wants a case.

1709	## How work lands
1710	
1711	The single source for the landing path, Sprites, the watcher and the
1712	CI gates is `docs/2026_10_11_THE_PIPELINE.md`; the section below is the
1713	doctrine it expands.
1714	
1715	- ALL WORK MOVES THROUGH SEVEN COMMANDS, and nothing else touches main:
1716	
1717	      sh tools/work new <name>   # a worktree ../avra-<name> off main, and its Sprite
1718	      sh tools/work run <cmd>    # run it on a GitHub runner (--sprite: the lane's Sprite), its exit status
1719	      sh tools/work test         # what this branch touches, on this lane's Sprite
1720	      sh tools/work land         # push, PR, arm auto-merge — no Sprite involved
1721	      sh tools/work status       # PRs and their merge state; each lane and its Sprite
1722	      sh tools/work sprites      # every Sprite at a glance; `--fix [name]` repairs
1723	      sh tools/work unbind       # end this lane's run, free its Sprite, keep the worktree
1724	      sh tools/work done --remove-worktree   # remove this lane too: ONLY with the owner's say-so
1725	
1726	  Main lives on GitHub (avra-lang/avra): squash merges, linear history,
1727	  no direct pushes. It requires the `test` check AND that a branch be up
1728	  to date with it, and auto-merge lands a green, current PR by itself,
1729	  one at a time. A local main
1730	  only follows `origin/main` (the reference-transaction hook refuses any
1731	  other update; a deliberate repair sets `AVRA_MAIN_OVERRIDE="<reason>"`).
1732	- THE PR IS THE TRAIN, AND THERE IS NO MERGE QUEUE (dropped 2026-10-11:
1733	  its only real value was testing `main` plus every PR ahead, which
1734	  "require up to date" gives back for free one PR at a time, while the
1735	  queue cost trains that tested many PRs at once — one red suite killed
1736	  them all — HEADGREEN batching and a rebase treadmill). A PR's `test`
1737	  check IS the gate, on the PR's own tree (`.github/workflows/
1738	  checks.yml`): fmt on its changed `.av`, idioms and suites over the
1739	  packages it TOUCHES, the compiler-dependent keepers, the seed check and
1740	  the affected packages' suites; a PR that touches no `.av`, no package
1741	  and no compiler source builds nothing. Before it builds anything it
1742	  runs the keepers that need NO COMPILER (`make keepers-static`, half a
1743	  minute), so a refusal one of them speaks stops on the PR. Because the
1744	  branch must be up to date, the tree it tests already holds `main`, so a
1745	  cross-PR interaction (two individually-green PRs
1746	  colliding on a latent bug) is caught on the later PR's own run. THE
1747	  COMPILER IS CACHED BY
1748	  ITS OWN SOURCE (`tools/compiler_paths.sh`): a tree whose compiler is
1749	  main's takes main's binary; otherwise the newest cached binary builds
1750	  the tree twice (the generation law), and one too old to read it — new
1751	  syntax, a new refusal about its own source — fails that build and the
1752	  tree BOOTSTRAPS from the committed seed. Main's own push run caches
1753	  the compiler every run starts from.
1754	- A LANE ITERATES WITH `make try`, NEVER `make avra`: it builds the
1755	  compiler with the STANDING `build/avra` into `build/avra-try` and never
1756	  replaces the builder, so its store stays warm (a leaf edit, ~4 s held
1757	  464/466) and `./avra-try <cmd>` probes the change. `make avra` is for
1758	  a change the compiler must READ to build itself — codegen, the front
1759	  end, a refusal about its own source — and before landing.
1760	- A PRE-COMMIT HOOK refuses staged `.av` that is not canonical; the fix
1761	  it prints is `build/avra fmt --write <files>`. Never `--no-verify`.
1762	- HEAVY RUNS GO ON SPRITES, ONE SPRITE A LANE: `sh tools/work run <cmd>`
1763	  from inside the worktree. `work new` binds a free Sprite (`work bind`
1764	  for a worktree that has none, `work unbind` frees it), and the lane's
1765	  tree and compiler stay warm there between runs. Bootstraps, whole
1766	  suites and censuses run there; the Mac keeps quick targeted checks and
1767	  anything macOS-only. ONE RUN PER SPRITE, EVERY STEP BOUNDED: `run`
1768	  answers the command's status, or 76 (busy), 70 (the compiler does not
1769	  build), 124/125 (a bound; `--for <minutes>` raises the command's), 137
1770	  (out of memory), 75 (the Sprite did not answer), 74 (the provider did
1771	  not answer) — and a failure's last line begins with the one of three
1772	  that failed: SPRITE, CONNECTION or COMMAND. A RUN BELONGS TO THE
1773	  SPRITE, NOT TO THE CONNECTION: a supervisor there keeps its output and
1774	  status and holds the Sprite awake while it lives, `run` only follows
1775	  it, and a dropped connection is followed again from the byte it stood
1776	  at — so Ctrl-C or `work stop` ends a run; a drop, a hangup or the
1777	  client being killed never does (it says so, and the next `run` answers
1778	  76 until `work attach` has followed it out); a run is as long as its
1779	  `--for` says, and the Sprite ends it at its bound whoever is
1780	  watching (`work attach` follows again, `work stop` ends it, `work
1781	  done` ends it with the lane). `sh tools/work sprites` shows all of
1782	  them in seconds.
1783	  A RUN ANSWERS ABOUT THIS WORKTREE OR NOT AT ALL: rsync carries files
1784	  to the Sprite, a file the worktree no longer has is removed there by
1785	  name, and the Sprite's manifest (every path and its hash) must equal
1786	  the worktree's before anything starts — else `SPRITE — sync:` and 75.
1787	  What a run wrote is left: `build/`, `.avra-cache`, anything git ignores.
1788	  WHAT ENDS A RUN EARLY IS MEMORY, NOT TIME: a twenty-minute exec holds,
1789	  chatty or silent, and thirty-two spinning processes leave a Sprite
1790	  answering in a second — but a Sprite says 16 GB and a balloon holds
1791	  half, more while it idles (3.3 to 7.3 GB were free to a run), there is
1792	  no swap, and under about 250 MB the whole machine answers nobody for
1793	  minutes. The Sprite's keeper ends a run at 600 MB (137), and every run
1794	  says what it had to start with. A SPRITE WITH NO SESSION AND NO HOLD
1795	  IS SUSPENDED WITHIN SECONDS, MID-WRITE IF NEED BE, which is why
1796	  nothing runs there detached without the hold; one silent for minutes
1797	  has lost its filesystem and is destroyed and created again
1798	  (provisioning is `run`'s first step, from `.github/ci/packages.txt`).
1799	  WHAT HOLDS A SPRITE AWAKE WITH NOBODY ATTACHED IS ITS TASKS API AND
1800	  NOTHING ELSE WE TRIED, measured over 400 s without contact: a task
1801	  refreshed each minute, no gap; a detached TTY session that prints, no
1802	  gap; a running service, a 372 s gap; outbound traffic, frozen at once;
1803	  an exec from outside every 20 s, one tick each. And a task's name is
1804	  lowercase letters, digits and dashes or the Sprite answers 400 — a
1805	  run is named after the machine that began it, capitals and all, so the
1806	  hold is asked under a name made to fit and ITS ANSWER IS READ. A run
1807	  that stood still says for how long in its own output, and `work
1808	  sprites` shows it beside how long the run has been quiet.
1809	- A BRANCH IS REBASED ONTO `origin/main` ONLY, never onto another
1810	  unlanded branch: that lands the other branch's work unverified. A
1811	  branch built on a stale local main moves with `git rebase --onto
1812	  origin/main main <branch>`, which carries only its own commits.
1813	- A PID IS CHECKED BEFORE IT IS KILLED. A recorded pid is reused once
1814	  its process exits; read `ps -o command= -p <pid>` first.
1815	- A TOOL IS RUN FOR REAL ONCE BEFORE IT BECOMES A DEFAULT. Fixtures
1816	  prove the logic; a live run proves the path (a 62 MB upload hit a
1817	  30 s client timeout that no fixture could reach).
1818	- A GATE FLOOR IS RELATIVE (N − k), NEVER AN ABSOLUTE COUNT: the total
1819	  moves when a branch deletes files, and an absolute floor then fails
1820	  correct work.
1821	- A CHANGE THE COMPILER CHECKS ABOUT ITS OWN SOURCE (a renamed type, a
1822	  new license form) lands as a BRIDGE first: main's compiler must build
1823	  the branch, because the seed and the gate's own build both use it.

1825	## Working discipline
1826	
1827	- NOTHING WE RUN TAKES MORE THAN A COUPLE OF MINUTES. Every command,
1828	  build, wait and poll is bounded to ~2 minutes; the ONE exception is a
1829	  full test run, which is ~5 minutes and runs on a Sprite. No `sleep`
1830	  chains, no 10–60 minute timeouts, no loop that polls `main` or a build
1831	  to infer progress. Break work into bounded steps: kick a long job off
1832	  as ONE bounded background command, do useful work, then check ONCE. A
1833	  `work wait` for a landing is bounded to a couple of minutes per call,
1834	  never an hour, and it reads the PR's state, never `main`.
1835	  A lane that blocks for minutes waiting is a defect in the lane, not
1836	  patience. (Owner rule, 2026-10-02: an 18-minute `sleep` loop waiting on
1837	  `main` deadlocked the merge queue — main could not move because that
1838	  lane's own PR was failing the train.)
1839	
1840	- GITHUB'S RUNNERS ARE THE ONLY GATE. `tools/gate_changed.sh` is the
1841	  gate's checks in one definition — the static keepers, `fmt --check`
1842	  on the changed `.av`, `check --baseline` on every affected package —
1843	  and checks.yml runs it on every PR, plus the compiler-dependent
1844	  keepers, the seed check and the affected packages' suites.
1845	  `tools/work land`
1846	  checks formatting alone, with the compiler the worktree already
1847	  holds, and asks no other machine; a lane that wants the whole gate
1848	  before pushing runs that script through `work run`.
1849	- A GREEN PR LANDS ITSELF, AND A STALE ONE IS REFRESHED. An armed PR
1850	  that falls behind `main` is updated by the watcher
1851	  (`tools/pr_watcher.py`, `gh pr update-branch`) so "up to date" is met
1852	  without a human; the watcher also arms a green PR, names a conflict
1853	  and cancels a closed PR's run. `work status` shows each PR's check,
1854	  its merge state and whether auto-merge is armed.
1855	- MEASURE, THEN CHANGE. `make census CMD="check <pkg>"` gives EXACT
1856	  retain/release/list-write counts and, with the per-caller tables,
1857	  who causes them; `AVRA_SAMPLE=<secs> sh tools/watch.sh 6000 ./avra
1858	  …` samples. Trust the census over the sample — and read
1859	  `sample`'s output with its tree characters (`+ ! : |`) in mind,
1860	  since parsing it as plain indentation reports the wrong fn.
1861	- A GEN-N VS GEN-N+1 DIVERGENCE IS FOUND BY TRACING, NEVER GUESSED.
1862	  `AVRA_QTRACE=1` prints one stderr line per query-kernel event —
1863	  every `Memo.ask` (family, arg, reuse/compute/cycle) and
1864	  `Memo.settle` (family, arg, fingerprint) in @std/relation's
1865	  engine/answers.av, every
1866	  `Binder.declare` (name, file) in features/namespace.av, every
1867	  failed `named_type` lookup in compiler/typing/declare.av, every
1868	  file a check PARSES (`Q parse <path>`, compiler/program.av), every
1869	  ATTEMPT a derivation makes (`Q attempt <turn> hold … reading <n>`,
1870	  compiler/derive.av) — behind
1871	  `avra_qtrace` (runtime/avra_runtime.c), inert without the flag.
1872	  Run both binaries on the SAME input with `AVRA_QTRACE=1`, confirm
1873	  each is deterministic against itself (diff two runs of the same
1874	  binary — must be empty), then diff the two traces: the FIRST
1875	  differing line names the query whose answer diverged first. Add a
1876	  probe at the divergent query's own site the same way — one
1877	  `qtrace(...)` call, removed once the cause is found.
1878	- WHICH COPY FORKED IS ANSWERED BY A CLONE LOG, NEVER BY READING THE
1879	  MECHANISM'S SOURCE. `AVRA_ALIAS_LOG=1` prints one stderr line per
1880	  ACTUAL `box_clone` (`avra_cell_unique`/`avra_slot_unique`,
1881	  runtime/avra_runtime.c's `alias_log_clone` — box_clone's only two
1882	  callers, so nothing clones outside this log) — the caller's
1883	  unslid return address (`atos -o <binary> <addr>` names it, no
1884	  `-l` needed) and the cloned box's ELEMENT COUNT. THAT COUNT IS
1885	  `a->len`, NEVER the header's `len`: every list, record and enum
1886	  payload is one `AvraArray` shape (`array_clone` treats them so),
1887	  and the header's `len` is that WRAPPER STRUCT's own fixed byte
1888	  size (40, `sizeof(AvraArray)`) — constant regardless of how many
1889	  fields or elements the box holds, so reading it answers "a box
1890	  was cloned" and never "how big". The first draft of this log
1891	  read the header and every clone in a 5.2M-line run showed length
1892	  40 or 32 — a tautology, not a finding.
1893	  AND DIFF THE LOGS BY SITE, NEVER BY PROFILE. avra-2y5c.5's gen-2
1894	  break was read from this log as an acquittal — "the same functions
1895	  at the same counts" in the good run and the broken one — while the
1896	  broken run held ONE line the good one did not: a 44-field clone at
1897	  `CheckCmd.run` (`mut ws = o.ws`, a workspace copied out of a record;
1898	  see A VALUE ITS OWN HOOKS CAPTURE, under Rules). Five million lines
1899	  that agree hide the one that forks.
1900	- A `check` HIT ON `.avra-cache` EXAMINES NOTHING, AND A SECOND
1901	  BINARY ON UNCHANGED SOURCE CAN SILENTLY HIT THE FIRST'S ENTRY.
1902	  `Workspace.checked`/`build_program` key their store by the
1903	  COMPILER'S OWN BYTES digest (`compiler_print`, compiler/build.av)
1904	  beside a `.avra-cache` directory, so building or checking with a
1905	  SECOND binary over the SAME source can read the FIRST binary's
1906	  kept warnings or kept binary outright — a differential build
1907	  (`AVRA_ALIAS_EMIT=0` vs `=1` over one source, or any two-binary
1908	  comparison) silently compares one binary's real run against the
1909	  other's cache hit, byte-identical checksums included. `rm -rf
1910	  .avra-cache` before every run whose ANSWER is being compared, not
1911	  only before the first. AND A CACHE FILLED BY A BINARY BUILT FROM
1912	  ANOTHER SHAPE IS NOT STALE — IT IS WRONG, AND IT TRAPS: bootstrapping
1913	  a tree through a temporary edit (a type carrying a second field so an
1914	  older builder could read it) left 3.6 GB of entries keyed by a
1915	  compiler whose IR assumed that layout, and the finished compiler read
1916	  them and lowered a suite that trapped on `index 1 is out of bounds
1917	  (length 1)` — deterministically, in a clean program, while the same
1918	  source in a cache-less tree was green. A stale entry costs a re-run;
1919	  one built from a different TYPE SHAPE costs an afternoon, so a lane
1920	  that bootstraps through any shape it will revert clears `.avra-cache`
1921	  before the run whose ANSWER it reads.
1922	- ONE HEAVY PROCESS AT A TIME, in the FOREGROUND, under the
1923	  watchdog: `sh tools/watch.sh 6000 make gate`. The machine is
1924	  shared with a loaded desktop and has panicked twice under this
1925	  tree — three concurrent `make test` runs once, and a background
1926	  gate with other compiler runs beside it (a WindowServer watchdog
